metadata.goal: Analyze trajectories from Bornholmsgat and the Great Belt observed during the same time window and identify their similarities and differences.
metadata.dataset_description: The main table contains same-period AIS-like trajectory points from two maritime corridors, with vessel type, reported draught, speed, and course. The vessel table contains one row per vessel and its corridor assignment.
metadata.header: Bornholmsgat and Great Belt Traffic Comparison

insight_list.insight: Vessels observed in Bornholmsgat have noticeably deeper reported draughts than those in the Great Belt; the maximum reported draught in the Great Belt subset is 14.0 m.

insight_list.question: How does reported vessel draught differ between vessels observed in Bornholmsgat and the Great Belt during the same time window?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the full draught distributions and their upper ranges by corridor rather than comparing only vessel counts.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

v = df[['vessel_id', 'corridor', 'draught']].drop_duplicates('vessel_id')
print(v.groupby('corridor')['draught'].agg(['count', 'median', 'max']))
v.boxplot(column='draught', by='corridor')
plt.title('Reported draught by corridor'); plt.suptitle(''); plt.ylabel('Draught (m)'); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Cargo vessels are the dominant vessel type in both corridors, forming the largest group in Great Belt traffic and also the largest group in Bornholmsgat traffic.

plot.title: Cross-Corridor Width of Aligned Traffic
plot.description: Each point is one aligned trajectory's median cross-corridor position in kilometres; transverse crossing tracks are reserved for the separate crossing-behavior analysis.

insight_list.question: How do the spatial concentration and apparent width of the main traffic tracks differ between the two corridors?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Project each corridor into local along-track and cross-track kilometre coordinates, then compare the occupied cross-track distributions of aligned passages on the same metric scale.
insight_list.code:
import math
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

d = df.copy()
axes = {'Bornholmsgat': ((14.10, 55.18), (14.75, 55.43)), 'Great Belt': ((10.92, 54.95), (10.94, 55.43))}
crossing_ids = {'bornholmsgat_vessel_16_track', 'bornholmsgat_vessel_17_track', 'bornholmsgat_vessel_18_track'}
rows = []
for corridor, (start, end) in axes.items():
 q = d[(d['corridor'] == corridor) & (~d['trajectory_id'].isin(crossing_ids))].copy()
 mean_lat = math.radians((start[1] + end[1]) / 2)
 x = (q['lon'].to_numpy() - start[0]) * 111.32 * math.cos(mean_lat)
 y = (q['lat'].to_numpy() - start[1]) * 110.57
 vx = (end[0] - start[0]) * 111.32 * math.cos(mean_lat); vy = (end[1] - start[1]) * 110.57
 length = math.hypot(vx, vy); cross = x * (-vy / length) + y * (vx / length)
 q['cross_km'] = cross
 medians = q.groupby('trajectory_id')['cross_km'].median()
 rows.extend((corridor, value) for value in medians)
w = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['corridor', 'cross_km'])
print(w.groupby('corridor')['cross_km'].quantile([.05, .5, .95]))
w.boxplot(column='cross_km', by='corridor', showfliers=False)
plt.suptitle(''); plt.title('Cross-corridor positions of aligned tracks'); plt.ylabel('Median cross-track position (km)'); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Several Bornholmsgat trajectories cross the principal traffic direction on near-perpendicular paths, while the Great Belt trajectories in the selected period remain aligned with the main north-south corridor and show no comparable transverse tracks.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

d = df.copy()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))
for ax, corridor in zip(axes, ['Bornholmsgat', 'Great Belt']):
 q = d[d['corridor'].eq(corridor)]
 for trajectory_id, group in q.groupby('trajectory_id'):
 ax.plot(group['lon'], group['lat'], color='navy', alpha=0.35)
 ax.set_title(corridor); ax.set_xlabel('Longitude'); ax.set_ylabel('Latitude'); ax.axis('equal')
plt.show()

insights: Vessels observed in Bornholmsgat have noticeably deeper reported draughts than those in the Great Belt; the maximum reported draught in the Great Belt subset is 14.0 m.
Cargo vessels are the dominant vessel type in both corridors, forming the largest group in Great Belt traffic and also the largest group in Bornholmsgat traffic.
Bornholmsgat contains several passenger-ferry trajectories, whereas the Great Belt contains only one passenger-ferry trajectory in the selected time window.
The Great Belt trajectories occupy a visibly narrower and more tightly concentrated main corridor, while Bornholmsgat trajectories spread across a wider traffic band around the principal route.

Several Bornholmsgat trajectories cross the principal traffic direction on near-perpendicular paths, while the Great Belt trajectories in the selected period remain aligned with the main north-south corridor and show no comparable transverse tracks.
summary: During the same observed time window, Bornholmsgat contains deeper-draught traffic, several passenger ferries, a wider spread of trajectory positions, and transverse crossing tracks. Great Belt traffic is also cargo-dominant but is concentrated in a narrower main corridor, contains very few ferries, and shows no comparable crossing behavior.
